title: Harness audit rule catalog
responsibility: Defines the standard audit limits and expresses supplied limits as human-readable rule summaries.

inputs.name: harnessRuleSummariesFor.limits
inputs.description: The HarnessRuleLimits object whose eight numbers are printed as upper bounds into the first eight summary lines: maxFileLines, maxFunctionLines, maxClassLines, maxMethodLines, maxNestingDepth, maxParameters, maxComplexity and maxClassesPerFile. It matters whenever summaries must state thresholds other than the standard harnessRuleLimits values, and because the function does no range or integer checks, every field must be a number and each supplied number appears in its summary line unchanged.

outputs.name: harnessRuleLimits
outputs.description: The standard audit thresholds exported as the constant harnessRuleLimits: 220 file lines, 55 function lines, 120 class lines, 35 method lines, nesting depth 4, 4 parameters, complexity 10 and one class per file, each an upper bound. It matters when the standard thresholds are needed, such as to derive the default harnessRuleSummaries.

outputs.name: harnessRuleSummaries
outputs.description: Rule summary strings computed once at module load as harnessRuleSummariesFor(harnessRuleLimits), so they always state the default limits: the eight limit sentences, a naming pointer, the naming rules, the module-grouping rules and the fixed structure, dependency and coverage guidance. It is the rule text to read for the standard limits, and it is a snapshot, so later changes to harnessRuleLimits do not change it.
examples: Files stay at or below 220 lines.
Functions stay at or below 55 lines.
Classes stay at or below 120 lines.
Methods stay at or below 35 lines.
Nesting stays at or below 4 levels.
Functions and methods take at most 4 parameters.
Cyclomatic complexity stays at or below 10.
Each file defines at most 1 class.
Use harness info naming and the scaffold guide before naming a module.

Naming: Helpers are pure camelCase functions; colliding SDK exports use <camelName>Helper while retaining the existing binding. Implementations belong in src/helpers/<responsibility>/<camelName>.ts; keep single-consumer functions in their owner folder.

outputs.name: harnessRuleSummariesFor
outputs.description: Ordered rule summary strings built from the supplied limits without range checks: eight sentences that print each numeric limit, then a naming pointer, the naming rules, the module-grouping rules and the fixed guidance. It matters when summaries must state thresholds other than the standard ones, and it inspects and changes no files.
